instantiated_cells.justification: Section 86117(a) requires reports be filed during the month following each calendar quarter, not annually.
Section 86117(a) specifies quarterly reporting (filed the month after each calendar quarter), not monthly reporting.
The statute sets a quarterly filing cycle and does not provide an alternative 'other' reporting frequency option for principals' periodic reports.
Section 86117(a) provides that reports required by §§ 86114 and 86116 shall be filed during the month following each calendar quarter.
Section 86117(a) requires quarterly reports rather than semi-annual reports.
Section 86117(a) uses a calendar-quarter reporting schedule, not a tri-annual legislative-calendar-linked schedule.
Lobbyist employer registration must include a description of the filer's business activity or nature and purposes, which discloses the nature of the business.
Principal filers under § 86115 must report total payments to each lobbying firm and total payments to lobbyists employed by the filer.
Section 86116 lists required contents of the principal periodic report and does not require disclosure of lobbying contacts or communications.
Section 86116(d) requires a description of the specific lobbying interests of the filer, which corresponds to general issues lobbied.
Section 86116(f) requires reporting each activity expense of the filer, and § 86111(a) defines activity expenses to include gifts and other benefits.
Section 86116(h)(1) requires reporting the total of all other payments to influence legislative or administrative action, including overhead expenses.
Section 86116(b) requires only the total amount of payments to each lobbying firm and does not require address/phone of contracted lobbyists.
The periodic report requires totals and lobbyist periodic reports for employed lobbyists, but it does not require listing the names of all lobbyists representing the principal.
Section 86116 contains no requirement to disclose major financial contributors to the principal.
Section 86116(a) requires disclosure of the filer's business address and telephone number in the periodic report.
The principal must describe specific lobbying interests under § 86116(d) but the statute does not require identification by bill number or legislation ID.
Section 86116(h)(1) requires reporting the total of all other payments to influence legislative or administrative action, capturing total expenditures beyond paid lobbyists and firms.
Principals must file periodic reports and disclose amounts paid to lobbying firms and to employed lobbyists, thus including salary/fees paid to lobbyists.
The statute generally requires totals (e.g., total payments to each lobbying firm; total payments to employed lobbyists; total other payments) rather than itemized line-items of spending.
Section 86116 does not require associations or representative groups to list names of all sponsors or members in the principal periodic spending report.
While § 86116(e) requires attaching periodic reports completed by each lobbyist employed, it does not require the principal report itself to list the lobbyists by name.
